title: How to find a $1M SaaS idea: the math, the 10% rule, and 2-week validation
summary: Tibo breaks a $1M SaaS down to roughly 350-700 paying customers, argues that copying the same idea-finding process as everyone else gives you the same ideas, and recommends building many products with strict 2-week validation windows. He gives four go/no-go questions and a fit test for choosing an idea.

principles.text: A $1M valuation is just 350 customers at $100/month or 700 at $50/month; the idea only needs to find that many consistent payers.
principles.quote: Your idea doesn't need to change the world. It just needs to find 350 to 700 people who will pay you consistently every month.

principles.text: If your idea-finding process matches everyone else's, you'll get the same ideas and compete with everyone who saw the same trend.
principles.quote: If you have the same process as everyone else, you'll have the same ideas as everyone else.

principles.text: Founders with deep industry experience see broken things others accept as normal; without that, use a build-many process instead.
principles.quote: Your industry knowledge makes you see something obviously broken that everyone else has accepted as normal.

principles.text: Expect about a 10% success rate on new products, so never go all in on one idea; build many instead.
principles.quote: Your success rate when creating new products will probably be 10% at best.

principles.text: Shipping one product per week forces you to ship over plan, get fast feedback, and discard the garbage cheaply.
principles.quote: It works because it forces you to ship instead of plan, get real feedback fast, and move past the 80% that will be garbage before it costs you a year of your life.

principles.text: Pick ideas that fit your skills, enjoyment, longevity, and the marketing channel you're naturally good at (SEO, content, ads, or sales).
principles.quote: if you hate writing and hate SEO, building a product that lives or dies on those channels will drain you fast.
